text:
incident-bot: ALERT — high 5xx rate observed for customer 'ZephyrCorp' private deployment (vpc-0a1b2c3d). Source: NLB in us-east-1a returning 502/504 to external gateway. Pager: oncall-eng@redwood.

oncall-eng: acked. I'm on it. Marking P1 and paging SRE. @sre-maya you're on secondary pager.

sre-maya: I see spike starting at 2026-03-15T02:07:xxZ. Dashboard: per-route 5xx from the NLB -> target group shows targets healthy but app logs show backend TLS handshake failures. Checking NLB health checks now.

netops-raj: pulling ELB info: `aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --names zephyr-nlb-prod` -> NLB active, 3 AZs. Health from ELB indicates targets healthy but client connections are failing at proxy layer. Could be SG or ephemeral port exhaustion on customer side.

customer-ops (ZephyrCorp): Confirming customers report product pages slow and some uploads failing. Impact: all API endpoints served via their private VPC NLB. They are seeing 502s in their app logs as well. No configuration changes on their side reported in the last 48h.

sre-maya: Running quick connectivity check from one of the dedicated pool hosts in same VPC: `curl -v http://10.12.34.56:8080/health` -> connection resets intermittently, TLS errors: `SSL: decryption failed or bad record mac`.

prod-eng-lin: Any recent cert rotations? We pushed a cert update to a shared TLS termination service yesterday but it shouldn't affect private NLB passthrough. Confirming no cert deploys scheduled against Zephyr.

eng-sre-tim: I'm pulling tcpdump on the instance: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'port 443' -c 200` and seeing client handshake -> server abort with `RST`. Suspect an intermittent firewall (SG) rule that is denying ephemeral ports back to the NLB. Also cross-checking source/dest port pairing.

netops-raj: Note: Zephyr uses a private hosted zone with internal-alias -> NLB alias. I see DNS TTL is low (60s) so unlikely stale DNS. But Route53 endpoints show multiple A records, one per AZ. One AZ's IP set looks different: `describe-network-interfaces` shows an extra ENI with a stale SG reference `sg-yyy` that shouldn't be attached. Noting potential mis-attachment during a recent customer change window.

incident-bot: DOCUMENT: Incident created. Severity=P1. Services impacted=zephyr-private-nlb (ingress/egress), potential customer-impact. Runbook: VPC NLB troubleshooting v2.

sre-maya: To avoid broad blast radius we won't modify Zephyr's SGs globally. Plan: 1) verify which ENI has mismatched SGs, 2) detach SG only from that ENI and re-attach correct sg-zeppelin, 3) drain NLB targets in that AZ and re-register after SG fix. If detaching is risky, we fallback to route-based mitigation (temporary AZ failover).

eng-sre-tim: I can take the handoff in 30m (need to sleep on-call). @sre-maya please add handoff note.

sre-maya: Handoff to @eng-sre-tim in 30m. Current: we've isolated problematic AZ (us-east-1a) where clients see highest error rate. All other AZs healthy.

customer-ops (ZephyrCorp): Any ETA for mitigation? Our sales team is getting pressure.

oncall-eng: ETA initial mitigation 20-30m. Will keep customer updated every 15m.

netops-raj: I'm preparing the targeted SG change. Command to inspect ENI and SGs:```aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1a --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].[NetworkInterfaceId,Groups]' --output json```

netops-raj: Found ENI eni-0f1e2d3c with groups `[ {GroupId: sg-yyy, GroupName: temp-access}, {GroupId: sg-zeppelin, GroupName: zephyr-backend} ]`. `sg-yyy` is a legacy temporary rule that opens broad egress to 0.0.0.0/0 for debugging — that could be causing asymmetric return-paths.

sre-maya: Because this is customer-specific, we must not remove sg-yyy without their explicit approval. Reaching out to Zephyr contact to authorize narrow change: remove `temp-access` and replace with `sg-zeppelin-ephemeral` which only allows NLB ephemeral ports back to targets.

customer-ops (ZephyrCorp): We did authorize temporary access last month for a limited time but didn't intend for it to remain. Approve removing `temp-access` if you limit to the specific ENI and only to port range 1024-65535 back to internal target subnet. :thumbsup:

eng-sre-tim: Good. I'll execute a minimal SG update and a drain of targets in that AZ. Steps: 1) create replacement SG `sg-zeppelin-ephemeral` with egress rule source=eni-0f1e2d3c, ports 1024-65535 -> internal; 2) modify ENI to attach new SG and detach `sg-yyy`; 3) deregister targets in TG for us-east-1a, wait 20s, reregister.

netops-raj: Preparing cloud CLI actions. Example create SG:```aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name sg-zeppelin-ephemeral --description "ephemeral return ports for zephyr" --vpc-id vpc-0a1b2c3d
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-zeppelin-ephemeral --protocol tcp --port 1024-65535 --cidr 10.12.0.0/16```

eng-sre-tim: Applying changes now (taking snapshot of ENI first). Will post commands and outputs.

(10m pause while change applied)

eng-sre-tim: Change applied: replaced sg-yyy on eni-0f1e2d3c with sg-zeppelin-ephemeral. Deregistering targets in `tg-00aabbcc` for us-east-1a.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: `eni-0f1e2d3c` SGs changed: removed sg-yyy, added sg-zeppelin-ephemeral. Target group tg-00aabbcc drained in AZ us-east-1a.

eng-sre-tim: After re-registering targets, I'm seeing reduced 502s. Metrics: 5xx rate down from 12% -> 1.2% in us-east-1a post-fix. No cross-tenant routing observed.

customer-ops (ZephyrCorp): We confirm user-facing error rate is dropping. Thanks. Please keep us informed on postmortem and whether this will be reverted.

sre-maya: Good catch. Root cause hypothesis: legacy debugging SG `sg-yyy` created asymmetric return path and caused TLS handshake resets when backend used different egress path. We'll validate with packet captures and full flow logs.

prod-eng-lin: Request adding an automated guard to detect legacy SGs attached to private-deployment ENIs (audit rule). Also flagging this for the release that manages customer onboarding automation.

eng-sre-tim: Next steps: 1) full pcap collection for the one-hour window (already saved to /var/tmp/pcap-1802001234.pcap), 2) VPC Flow Logs export for ENI for the same window, 3) postmortem with customer and change to onboarding docs to ensure `temp-access` SGs are ephemeral with TTL.

sre-maya: Handoff complete to @eng-sre-tim. I'm available for followups. Closing active paging.

incident-bot: RESOLUTION_NOTE: Temporary SG removed and replaced with narrow ephemeral SG. Impact mitigated and rates returned to baseline. P1 -> resolved. Postmortem scheduled 2026-03-16T15:00Z.

eng-sre-tim: We'll avoid broad automation that flips SGs without customer consent. Action owner: @netops-raj to create audit rule; @prod-eng-lin to add onboarding check.

customer-ops (ZephyrCorp): Appreciate the swift handling. Please share the postmortem and the exact changes for audit.

incident-bot: THREAD_SUMMARY: customer ZephyrCorp experienced NLB 5xx due to legacy SG causing asymmetric traffic. Targeted SG replacement on specific ENI in us-east-1a mitigated incident. No other customers impacted. Follow-ups: audit rule, onboarding check, postmortem.
